utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning, sir. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to turn, Mr. Keskovski, now to the 12th of August, Sunday, the 12th of August, and I'd like to ask you, if you can recall, where you were the morning of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The morning of the 12th of August, around 9.00, 10.00, we took the president from his residence to his office, to the cabinet of the Republic of Macedonia. I stayed in my workplace in my office, preparing the activities for the successful preparations for the signing of the Ohrid Agreement, which took place at the residence of the president of the Republic of Macedonia on the 13th, the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Keskovski. We'll take that one step at a time. First, you said that: "We took the president from his residence." Who is "we"? Was there anyone else with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the people from the sector of security of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know who is driving the president usually? I think you indicated yesterday, but if could you recall that.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first driver of the president was Mr. Mladenov Aco, usually.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall now whether that was Mr. Mladenov who was driving the president on that day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, Mladenov.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And now can you recount what happened when you arrived at the office of the president's cabinet, that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The morning, when we came to the cabinet of the president, as I started to say, I went to my office in order to start the preparations for the Ohrid Framework Agreement. Before arriving, the president asked for my mobile phone to make some standard calls which he made on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did the president at some stage ask to see you or did you go to see the president on your own at some stage that morning?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the day, that is to say, prior to starting the meeting which I scheduled regarding the organisation of the Ohrid Framework Agreement with the whole group, the whole sector for the security of the president, the president called me in my office and told me to come see him immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what did he tell you, if anything, at that point?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president called me in, told me that in Ljuboten and in the area of Ljubanci there have been some activities, and said that he wants to establish contact immediately with the minister of interior, Mr. Ljube Boskoski. On his order, I attempted to find the minister; however, I was unable to establish contact with him. This is a telephone number which I had memorised in my mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just a second, we'll get to that point in a second, Mr. Keskovski. Did the president first tell you who he had gotten that information from, about things happening in Ljuboten and Ljubanci? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not tell me who he received this information from. He asked me whether I had the possibility to establish contact with Mr. Tarculovski. I tried to reach him, too, on my mobile phone, but I was unable to do so at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated that he then asked you to try to get in touch with Mr. Boskoski. Could you -- or did he tell you why he wanted to talk to Mr. Boskoski at that point?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning of the 12th, there was information about an angry mass of people, a crowd in the area of Radisani, who were, so to say, armed with iron rods and other weapons of domestic character from household items, ready to charge and to deal with the terrorist groups stationed in the village of Ljuboten. Due to these reasons, because these were ordinary people, civilians, they could have had direct contact with ordinary civilians of Albanian ethnicity causing conflict and skirmishes on an ethnic basis. All of this could have put into question the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. And due to these reasons, the president asked for Mr. Boskoski and attempted to establish contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And could -- you started explaining the efforts that you made to get in touch with Mr. Boskoski. Could you explain what steps you took to contact Mr. Boskoski and whether you were successful in doing so.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to reach Mr. Boskoski on the telephone and the telephone numbers I had at my disposal, but I was unable to do so, because during the weekend our office did not work with the standard team that works during the working week. The president pointed that I should ask at the office of the prime minister to try to establish contact with Mr. Boskoski, that the office of the prime minister should tell me how I might try to get in touch with him. I did so, and I spoke with Mr. Ljusev who was at his work post. He gave me several telephone numbers from the immediate entourage of Mr. Boskoski. I believe this was specifically the number of the driver of Mr. Boskoski. I called this number, cell phone. I established contact with the driver and asked him whether the minister was with him and whether he is available for a telephone conversation. He told me that he was. And in the first voice contact I had with the minister during that time, I told that the president wanted to speak with him. I handed the phone over to the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just a second before we go to that, Mr. Keskovski. Did you exchange any word, did you say anything to Mr. Boskoski, or did he say anything to you at that point?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. According to the standard procedure, I noted that Mr. Boskoski was on the telephone. As I said previously, this was the procedure. When the president will speak to someone on the other end of the line, I have to know who is it with. There was no other conversation between Minister Boskoski and myself, just the regular pleasantries, "Good morning, Good afternoon, Mr. Minister, the president of the Republic wishes to speak with."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did the minister and the president then talk to each other?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The president explained to Mr. Boskoski the information he conveyed to me as well, which I already elaborated, regarding the situation in the area of Radisani and the possibility of radicalisation and escalation of the, so to say, protests or attacks that could escalate into an interethnic clashes between civilians of the Republic of Macedonia of Macedonian and Albanian ethnicities, and that in the interest of calming the situation down, in the interest of the following day's signing of the Framework Agreement which was of extreme significance at that moment for quieting the crisis which had occurred in the Republic of Macedonia, the president ordered Mr. Boskoski to go there and with his authority to calm down the crowds and to forbid them from going into the village of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you able, or were you aware at that time, where Mr. Boskoski was when you managed to contact him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot know where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you able, even if approximately, to recall what time of the day it would have been, approximately, when you managed to make phone contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this happened prior to the meeting I had scheduled with the sector for the security of the president, with the whole team. I believe this was before 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall now what you did for the rest of the day, the 12th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I had previously mentioned, during that day, I was working on the preparations of all the guests that were due to arrive the following day for the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement, including VIPs from the international communicate such as Mr. Javier Solana, Mr. George Robertson, Mr. Leotard, Mr. Pardew, several ambassadors, and about 200 journalists from various media that had announced their presence, and the leadership of the Republic of Macedonia who were to be the guests of the president, so to say, because this was due to take place at the residence of the president. This is a very major activity. I presume you can assume the scope of this event, both from a security and from a protocol point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems that we are all encountering some problems with the transcript. We will just carry on. If there is a problem perhaps with our colleague or yourself, we will be happy to stop if instructed by you. But at this stage, I'm able to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have one source of transcript but not the other. I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The problem, Your Honour, is I believe I am the only one among the three of to us have access to the transcript. I'm able to carry on, if Your Honour wishes, but my colleagues are not able to log on their transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we should press on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for the transcript, at page 6, line 10, "Leotard" would be L-E-O-T-A-R-D.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you know or do you know, Mr. Keskovski, where the president was during the rest of the day, the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the morning hours, the president was in his office, up until the late evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall where your phone was at the time, or whether it was at all times with you, your mobile phone?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the whole team arrived at the residence, the president requested one of the mobile phones to make calls which were standard on a daily basis. This is something that happened not just on that day but every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And yourself, Mr. Keskovski, do you recall whether during that day, the 12th of August of 2001, you've made -- you've had any call or made any attempt to contact Mr. Tarculovski. You've indicate already that when discussing with the president you made a number of attempts to do so. Can you recall now whether you made any such attempts at other times during that day?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was seeing the president, I attempted to reach Mr. Tarculovski; however, I was not able to establish contact with him, and on that day I had no contact with Mr. Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask you about a different time. Do you recall when, approximately, Mr. Tarculovski came back to work after these events?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tarculovski returned to his work duties. Immediately after escorting the first lady, he continued with his regular tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at that time, Mr. Keskovski, did you have any reason to believe that Mr. Tarculovski had done anything illegal or criminal?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no reasons for me to suspect anything of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you able to say whether, upon his return, Mr. Tarculovski reported to the president; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And later in time, did you learn or did you learn at any point that, from any source, that there were allegations that Mr. Tarculovski had taken part in the action? Did you hear those stories later?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about this after ten months after this event. When this case began to be scrutinized by the public, I learned this from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And upon learning this, did you ask Mr. Tarculovski about those reports?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were not reports. These were information which were disseminated in the public at that moment. I asked him on one specific occasion whether what the papers were saying was true. He told me that these were speculation and that they were untrue.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know if the president asked Mr. Tarculovski about those?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were together when I asked him. I'm not sure whether he knew about this previously or what he knew, but we were together when I asked him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you say, "We were together," do you mean to say that when you asked Mr. Tarculovski, the president was also present?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not officially. This was in regular movement as we were walking. This wasn't a special call for Mr. Tarculovski. This wasn't a special meeting so that I could ask him about these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did the president at any stage give you an indication that he wished or wanted this matter to be looked into?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not once.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I have one last question, I believe, or one last set of questions. Are you aware of any case or cases of police officers being amnestied for crimes committed during the crisis; and, if so, how did you learn about that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about one member of the Ministry of Interior who was amnestied. I met him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I have several questions for this witness. I would ask the Court for a few minutes of patience so that I may prepare myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: My name it is Antonio Apostolski, and together with my colleague, Jasmina Zivkovic, we are the Defence counsel of Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Before I begin with my questions, I would like to turn your attention to the fact that you and I speak the same language and are able to easily understand each other. However, I would ask you to pause and wait for the interpretation of my questions, as well as your answers, so as to enable the Trial Chamber and all present in the courtroom to follow my questioning and your testimony in an easier fashion. Do you understand what I have said to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned that, as chief of security of President Boris Trajkovski, you were privy to a lot of information related to the security of the security forces and of the terrorist group NLA. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Also, yesterday, you indicated that upon the order of President Trajkovski, you were in several areas where the Macedonian security forces carried out activities for eliminating the terrorist group NLA. You said you mentioned Vaksince, in the area of Tetovo, and in Aracinovo. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that following the activities of the Macedonian security forces for eliminating the terrorist group NLA in Tetovo in March, on the 25th and 26th of May in Vaksince, the members of the NLA in uniforms disappeared and they intermixed with the local Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this was part of the tactics of the terrorist group NLA?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that after this it was necessary to -- for the police to have paraffin glove tests to establish whether these persons were terrorists or civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take part in this and the testing of the terrorist groups, whether or not they took part in the activities. This was work of the regular police forces that were specialised in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: While you were in these areas you mentioned earlier, did you have the authorisation to issue orders to the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was sent to report from the areas about the situation and the activities for elimination and everything else related to the operations of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When the president sent Johan Tarculovski to Ljubanci and Ljuboten, did you give him or have you heard that he gave him the authorisation to issue orders to the Macedonian security forces within this region?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't heard him give him the authority to issue orders. I only heard that he gave him the order to inform him about the situation in the region. This is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Is it correct that, in July and August 2001, the terrorist group NLA systemically carried out ethnic cleansing in the areas populated with Macedonian and Serbian ethnic population and especially in the Tetovo, Kumanovo, and Skopje regions, which resulted in murders, beating, and kidnapping of non-Albanians and some them are not found until the present day?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I believe that calls for speculation on the part of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you haven't established any foundation of knowledge for such wide-sweeping question, Mr. Apostolski. If the witness has personal knowledge about any of these matters, you need to bring that out first, before you can ask him to answer a question of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked this question since the witness was a direct witness to the events of 2001 in the Republic of Macedonia. So I thought that he would be able to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the fact that he was living and involved in some respects with events in 2001 isn't enough to qualify him to speak about the matters you have asked about, which are extremely wide-sweeping. If you want to get from him particular knowledge about any of the matters dealt with in your question, you need to have him establish his knowledge and the source of it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I will then put it differently. I will reframe the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yesterday, in your evidence, you stated that it was the president himself, Boris Trajkovski, who requested that some individuals were involved in his entourage [as interpreted]. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Security.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that irrespectively of his ask, you, yourself, made the assessment of the individuals who were to take care about the security of the president and his family?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a regular procedure in the Ministry of Interior; and, of course, it is only natural to check the persons who will be responsible for the security of the president by -- checked by all security structures who have data and are able to make such assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you do that also with regards to the individual Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did this with regards to all individuals, with no exception, so that included Mr. Johan Tarculovski as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did Mr. Johan Tarculovski have a criminal background?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't have had. If he has had one, he wouldn't have been included in the security of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you check on his psychological and physical fitness, or was there any committee taking care of that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is done at the moment the employment is entered into with the Ministry of Interior. All members and authorised officials of the Ministry of Interior go through a regular procedure of test of psychological and physical fitness, and a certificate on that is issued so that they are able and to the conclusion that certificate is that the individual is able to perform the duties within the Ministry of Interior. It concerns authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So my conclusion that Johan Tarculovski was selected for the security based on the personal wish of the president Boris Trajkovski and that he met all the prerequisites necessary for that post would be correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Johan Tarculovski was in charge of the security for the first lady also during her official and private trips abroad?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know whether he speaks the English language?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe he does, since several times I have sent him together with the first lady abroad. Since it is the minimum prerequisite, the employee needs to speak at least one foreign language to be able to communicate with other security services that need to welcome you and escort you in the country where are you travelling and you need to cooperate with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that before the trips abroad, the trips of the first lady abroad, you had contacts with the foreign services that, together with her personal security, would be responsible for her security and safety?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have never received any criticism with regards to the work of Johan Tarculovski by the foreign services, security services, that you cooperated with?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never received any criticism with regards to the work of Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that when travelling abroad to provide for the security of the first lady, Mr. Johan Tarculovski carried weapons on him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the host country, in its regulations allows that, yes, since the different states have different regulations; but, generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Johan Tarculovski also travelled with Mr. Boris Trajkovski during the trips abroad when the first lady was accompanying the president. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Johan accompanied the president and the first lady to Italy, when the president had a meeting with the Pope?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Johan Tarculovski also travelled to Norway when President Trajkovski received the peace award?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Mr. Johan Tarculovski went to China with the president and the first lady, when the President Trajkovski visited China?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And within one question, I will enumerate several states where Mr. Johan Tarculovski had travelled with the first lady only, when he escorted her during her trip. We have here Great Britain, Germany, Italy, Croatia, Bulgaria, and Greece. Could you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had the list of all such trips where he performed duties abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And, so, none of these states, or rather, the agencies, services, security services, had any complaints against the work of Mr. Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated already, no, they haven't had.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Johan Tarculovski was involved in all major operations to secure meetings in the Republic of Macedonia as well, where the organiser was the president, Boris Trajkovski? Could you please tell us about that, if you are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would correct this. This is not meetings; these are summits. Yes. In all major operations organised by the security service of the president and in coordination with all the other security services an agencies in the Republic of Macedonia, we've had several events where we had more than 15 heads of states as guests. This is how they're called because somewhere the president is the head of the state, but somewhere the prime minister is the head of the state. And in all these operations, Mr. Tarculovski had his tasks and he performed them successfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether it's correct that the residence of the president, Boris Trajkovski, is located near PSOLO; that is, the Police Station for Security of Individuals and Facilities?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The residential part of President Trajkovski was and still is at the moment the residence of the president of the Republic of Macedonia, and it shares the same garden with the villa. This is how it is called in Macedonia. It shares the same complex with the residence of the prime minister of the Republic of Macedonia and the guest residence. This is one complex of high-level state facilities, and it is set some 300 to 400 metres away from the PSOLO station and it is strategically designed to be like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you have any requested made of PSOLO as head of the security service for Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in communication with PSOLO. It was standard communication within the standard framework because PSOLO was guarding the entrance to that complex, the gate - how should I call it? - the entrance into the complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You're referring to the gate of the residence?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the entrance gate into the entire complex of residence. I'm now speaking about the residences of both the president and the prime minister. They are within the same complex. They shared the same garden.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that PSOLO also secured the parliament building where the office of the president of the state is?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: PSOLO is a police station for security of persons and facilities and diplomatic and consular representative offices. It means that it is in charge of external physical security of all those facilitates within the territory of the Republic of Macedonia. So it secured the parliament building as well, the government building as well, and the residential part of the villa in Ohrid that is the president's villa, and all the other vital facilitates in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would that mean that the employees in the President Boris Trajkovski's security needed to frequently visit the PSOLO police station?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, if they needed to have contact with the polices station with regards to this part of physical security of the residential part, and possibly the cabinet. This is among the standard daily activities. They don't have or they need a precise order for this. These are everyday activities, regular, standard. They're not special activities. They are standard activities, every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So it is your evidence that it could be a daily activity of a member of staff to visit this police station?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the security inspector, if a member of the security feels the need and believes that he needs to get in touch with PSOLO and feels that there is a need to have a higher level discussion at PSOLO regarding the security that they provide, then, yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now move to deal with another topic. Yesterday, you testified that the president of the Republic of Macedonia issued an order on the 5th of August, 2001, and he ordered, among other things, that the road between Tetovo and Jezince be mopped up from the NLA terrorists. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I spoke about it yesterday, but I remember the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know about this event?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know about this event, even the public learned about there event.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So my next question was to be: Is it correct that this order was disclosed to the media by one of the high military officers and was published at the national television, A-1, and this is why it was impossible to follow this order?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was published at the A-1 television. But who disclosed the information to the A-1 television, I really couldn't know. I can only tell you that the order of the president reached the chief of the General Staff; and, after that, I don't know what the procedure is to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have information that the president of the Republic of Macedonia was greatly disturbed and angry because of this, or after this, since, if I could put it like this, this information leaked to the media?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, he was, because any information that is strictly confidential, of course an official would be upset if that leaked to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You stated, yesterday, that after the events at Karpalak, the president of the Republic of Macedonia dismissed chief of the General Staff, Pande Petrovski on the 9th of August, 2001. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 726.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see, in the screen in front of you, the Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia? Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is reads Official Gazette of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The date is Friday, 9th of August, 2001. And beneath it, it is written, "Decree number 38," and it is written there: "On the basis of Article 18, paragraph 1, line 18 of Defence Law, General Lieutenant-Colonel Pande Alekso Petrovski is dismissed from the duty of the chief of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia." Then it continues: "The dismissal from duty took place on the 9th of August, 2001. This decree is to enter force immediately," and it is signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski. Does this corroborate your evidence that General Lieutenant-Colonel Pande Petrovski was dismissed from the office of the chief of the General Staff of the Republic of Macedonia on the 9th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said this yesterday during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I seek to tender this document into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D84, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you have information that the president received information all the time from the intelligence sector of the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did he use those to make decisions?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also security structures, including those within the Ministry of Defence and of the Ministry of Interior, the intelligence agency and external friendly services that were active in the Republic of Macedonia sent information to the President Trajkovski, information of various nature; and on the basis of all those information, the president, analysing those, undertook measures and made decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 2D42, Exhibit 2D42. Page N002-4321-0129, that is the Macedonian version; and the English page is 2D05-0386.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: That is a daily log of information received on the 10 and 11 of August, 2001, of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, security sector.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just have it shown on the -- on my screen, or actually, could I have only the Macedonian version on my screen because it is tiny and I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom on the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see number 13, on the 10th of August, at 1655, G-2 has recorded that information was received that a group of around 100 individuals need to start from the region of village of Matejce towards the villages of Ljubanci, Ljuboten, Brodec, and Kodra Fura in order to attack the positions of the defence security forces? Would the president have this information at his disposal?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. These are primarily intended for the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the Macedonian page N002, of the same document, N002-4321-0125; English page 2D05-0383.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. I wonder if perhaps we could show the English page so the Prosecution can follow along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness needs document in Macedonian. It should be possible for the witness to have one screen display and others to have another.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just in case, I will read it for the transcript so that we know what it written here. It is the same log-book, just a different page of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You see in line starting with 8?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it: "10 of August, 1645."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The information comes from the MOI, Mirkovci police station. It is a telegram on the 10 August, 2001. "At 1530, a patrol of Mirkovci police station, stationed above the village of Ljuboten, and the authorised official, Todorov Dusan, informed us that in the village of Ljuboten, at the sweep between the school and the graveyard on the left-hand side of the road, in the in the houses of Zendelovski family, they noticed three individuals wearing black uniforms and armed with automatic weapons."

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would the president have this information at his disposal as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a telegram sent to all organs dealing with the security issues. I said, previously, that he received information. We received in general information from all security services active on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia. We received them continuously.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may have one moment of your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. Keskovski.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: My name is Antoinette Issa, and I represent the Prosecution today. Now, Mr. Keskovski, you testified in your examination-in-chief that in December of 1999, you became the head of the Macedonian security sector for the president. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And in -- on 28 May 2001, you were promoted to senior inspector for the security of the president, and you were given an increase in your salary by the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not a promotion. This is a new systemization of 2001. They're the same work posts with new titles, so to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But you were given an increase in your salary. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a small increase.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And this was shortly after Ljube Boskoski became the minister of the interior, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct, because there was when the new systemization was passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And you stayed in that position until 7 June 2002. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And, at that point, you were, once again -- or I should say, at that point, you were given a promotion to the -- a position of deputy assistant of the minister of the interior for security matters, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And then, on 13 August of 2002, which is approximately two months later, you were then assigned to the post of the assistant to the director for the DBK by Minister Boskoski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But then, on the 5th of November, 2002, you went from being the assistant director to the DBK to being reassigned as inspector regarding Islamic fundamentalism. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You weren't -- wasn't there a decision made by then-Minister Hari Kostov to reassign to you a position of independent inspector on prevention from Islamic fundamentalism and religious extremism in the department of the DBK in Tetovo?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. This is an error in his procedure. Sometimes, wishes are greater than reason. According to the labour law, I was as of 10th of August, 2002 up until 31st of January, 2003; and according to the labour law, heads do not have the authorisation to give reassignment decisions for a person who has been on leave or who is on vacation. If you look at my dismissal note, you will see that I was given a note of dismissal at the position of assistant to the minister for the UBK.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you develop the question, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply, I believe a word or a couple of words have been missed in page 25, line -- it should probably be in line 5, where we understand Mr. Keskovski says where he was or what he was doing between 10 August and 31st of January, but I think he specified that later in the answer. Just for the record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry, Ms. Issa. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Keskovski, regardless of whether the decision was in conformity of the labour law, wasn't there a decision made by Minister Hari Kostov at the time to reassign to you that position of inspector on prevention for Islamic fundamentalism to take effect on November 5, 2002?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive any decision of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, if we can distribute the Prosecution binders at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Now that the binders have been distributed, I would ask you to please turn to page 31.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It should be -- and I would ask that this perhaps be pulled up on e-court, please. It is page 31. It should be 31 in e-court in the English and Macedonian, and the ERN number is N006-7461 for tab 50, 65 ter 1139. I should have said what the 65 ter number was first for Madam Registrar. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I would ask you, sir, to go to your second binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number? Tab number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Tab 50, please. I would ask to you turn to page N006-7461, which should be at page 31 of the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps, if I might ask the assistance of Mr. Usher to the witness, if needed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now you see there, Mr. Keskovski, there's a decision that is dated November 5, 2002. What it says is that: "Zlatko Keskovski," if you look at the first paragraph underneath the word "decision," "who, until now, was employed as assistant to the director for operational matters and coordination in the cabinet of the director of the UBK at the Ministry of Interior, is assigned to a place of duty, independent inspector on prevention from Islamic fundamentalism and religious extremism, in the regional department of the UBK commencing as of the date 5/11/2002." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you turn the page, you see that that's a decision that was made by then-Minister Hari Kostov, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And, Mr. Keskovski, you tendered your resignation on 7 November 2002, two days after this decision was made. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tendered a request to resign on the 7th of July, 2002 [as interpreted], and this -- this is a decision of the 5th of May [as interpreted]. But as one can see from the document, there is no signature on this document signifying that I received this document, which is an obligatory procedure in the ministry when receiving a new decision for reassignment to a new workplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if we're looking at the e-court copy, Mr. Keskovski, it appears that, just to clarify the record, there is a signature on the document, and it is signed by Minister Hari Kostov with the ministry's stamp, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was speaking about my signature, a signature signifying my receipt of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that you didn't receive this document, that you were -- despite the fact that you were supposed to start in this new position on the 5th of November; and then you resigned on 7 November, 2002, but you say you never received this document. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. And I'm looking at this for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you please turn to page 28 of that same document, the same exhibit, which is N006-7458 for e-court purposes. Do you see that? Are you there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, isn't that your request for your resignation from the ministry, which is dated 7 November 2002? Isn't that your signature there, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. And, as you're able to see, it says "assistant director in the UBK." Therefore, I was still at that position, and I'm seeking a resignation from the post of assistant to the director in the directorate for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But that was, nevertheless, two days after the decision of Minister Hari Kostov was to take effect. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not so, because Hari Kostov, for the first time, entered the Ministry of Interior on the 7th of November, 2002. When I was tendering my resignation, his wish was not taken into consideration that he issue me a new decision for reassignment. You can see this in my resignation, again signed by Hari Kostov who gives permission to my resignation from the position of assistant to the director of the UBK [as interpreted]. This means that he has invalidated his own signature and is allowing me now to leave from the position of assistant director in the directorate for security and counter-intelligence. This is the same minister in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Keskovski, that was only two days after the initial decision was made by Hari Kostov. Are you suggesting that when you resigned two days after this decision was made that was a mere coincidence and it had nothing to do with Hari Kostov's decision?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My decision was submitted prior to Mr. Kostov requesting that I be reassigned because it's his first day at work; and on his first day of work, he immediately distributed such decisions. I had tendered my resignation previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say "on his first day at work, he immediately distributed such decisions," that's because when a new minister comes into office and perhaps does not have the same political affiliations with certain members of the previous ministry, he may demote people. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'd have to clarify what you mean by this term.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: The term "demote," is that the term you're referring to, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To replace means that an assistant director, such as my position, you can be the head of a directorate; but to demote, or as translation goes degrade, can indicate something else. It could mean political vindication, perhaps. This is something altogether different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll use a different description then, Mr. Keskovski. It's possible that when a minister, a new minister comes into office, he transfers individuals or members of the previous ministry, such as yourself, to positions that were of lower rank, or grade perhaps, than the position than you used to be in. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but two to three levels at maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you resigned from the ministry, you knew that you would be demoted, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not so. I tendered my resignation due to moral reasons, without any knowledge that I would receive another decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So the two-day gap between your -- Hari Kostov's decision and your resignation was a mere coincidence, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kostov signed the decision on the 5th; while on the 5th, he did not step even into the Ministry of Interior. You can establish this if you speak with various structures in the Republic of Macedonia who can verify this with valid documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm conscious of the time, and I was about to move into other area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the first break. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is informed there is a procedural matter. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As it's clear, I am obviously in a position to begin my cross-examination today. However, in light of the additional material that we received yesterday and just in passing, there was some additional material that came out in the cross-examination that was carried out by Mr. Apostolski. We will, of course, use this afternoon to attempt to prepare as much as possible for the continuation tomorrow. However, I didn't -- I wanted to inform the Chamber that there is a possibility that we would be asking for an extra session to assist in our preparation to perhaps obtain additional material that we may need to add to our exhibit list in light of all of this new material that has come out during the direct examinations. I wanted to advise the Chamber of that at the start of my cross-examination, but I didn't want to do it in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Ms. Issa. Do I understand correctly that you're planning to proceed now and able to do so, but it may happen in the course of the day that you have to seek an adjournment over until tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- to enable to you prepare more adequately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for letting us know that in anticipation. It may not emerge, of course, but we will proceed now and you will judge whether you reach the position you're anticipating.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. Your Honours. I wish to apologise for the last paragraph I said in the previous session to the Prosecutor's office. I remembered during the break about the activities during that time, that I was questioned about. So I can confirm that, if memory serves, Mr. Kostov started performing his office on the 5th of November, 2002, since for five years I didn't have the need to remember this event. But during the recess, I refreshed my memory and I remembered that Mr. Kostov started performing the office on the 5th of November, and this is why I wish to apologise for the mistake that I have made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Issa, you're ready to move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Keskovski, I would ask you to please go to page 12 of the same document we were dealing with earlier, which is 65 ter 1139, your personnel record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the e-court, it's page 12, and the ERN is N006-7442.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, on the 5th of November, after that decision was made by Hari Kostov, you were asked to return some equipment and a weapon that were issued to you by the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't received this request or a reprimand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I would ask you, then, Mr. Keskovski, to turn, please, to page 17, ERN number N006-7447. This is a document dated 14 October 2003, where the Ministry of Interior is still looking for you to return your official identification. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I see here is what is written. I haven't received this either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, as a member of the Ministry of Interior, Mr. Keskovski, didn't you know that you were required to return the property of the ministry upon your resignation?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We have mutual obligations. I have obligations towards the ministry, and the ministry has obligations towards me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you turn, please, to page 12 in your document, which is N006-7442 -- actually, if I can ask you to turn to page 13, N006-7443, there's a further letter that says that -- which is dated the 29th of June, 2005, requesting and obliging you to -- or, actually, that's a letter from you requesting your material or your booklet, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. The booklet is requested so that I can exercise my constitutional right, rights guaranteed by the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia. As it is indicated, it is my request to exercise my basic human rights guaranteed by the Republic of Macedonia, and I quote to the Article of the labour law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So, clearly, at that time, Mr. Keskovski, at least in 2005, you were clearly aware of the obligations, at least in respect of how it pertained to the ministry's obligations to you. You asked for your property back, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I phoned the Ministry of Interior several times before, I indicated that we had this problem with regards to my exercising of basic human rights, right to employment and social insurance, for me and my family. At that point in time, my child was three years old. I was informed that the Ministry of Interior will not return me the employment booklet up until we fully reconcile our relations, but this reconciliation or restoration of obligations is the competence of Basic Court I. The Ministry of Interior does not have the right, regardless of any need they might have, to hold on to my employment booklet. Without it, I couldn't exercise basic human rights guaranteed with the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia and also by several international legal instruments.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you feel the right to hold on to the ministry's property then, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise for objecting. But I think if my colleague wants to put that question to the witness, she should first time inquire whether, in fact, he held on to any such material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness will be able to answer that, if that is the position, Mr. Mettraux. Carry on, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you feel that you had a right to hold on to property that belonged to the ministry, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you referring to precisely?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, let's go to page 9 of your personnel record, number ERN range -- or ERN N006-7439. There's an information which is dated 11 July 2005, one month after you sent the letter to the ministry demanding your booklet to be returned, which states that you still hadn't returned the property of the ministry, and it describes the nature of the property that hadn't been returned. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to read it, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps we can go through it together. It relates to a request which was dated 30th June 2005 that was submitted by you, and then it deals with the list of items which are described as technical means and equipment of employees of the ministry; and that you were informed to return this property and you hadn't returned it. And if we see here, the nature of the property includes the official ID of the ministry, mobile telephones, automatic rifle, handcuffs, ammunition for a couple of revolvers, a pistol. And if you turn the page, it refers to a bullet proof jacket, for example, and so on. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the body of the letter, it says, on the second page, at page 10 in your hard copy: "We would like to inform that already we had sent a warning before charges on returning the official ID dated 14 October 2003." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And it is signed by the assistant to the minister, Vesna Dorevska. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: As a member of the ministry, Mr. Keskovski, weren't you required to uphold the law?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards to the list indicated in this document, and I will say again, this is a document that I see for the first time now, because you omitted this part which states that all delivery notes had returned. The service was not proper. The ministry has not found me. So, before I finish, I will say that these were all means or instruments that I had during performing my duty as the head of the security for the president of the state. And you can see here that I had two Nokia, to Ericsson mobile phone, three Nokia chargers, holder for Nokia, holder for Ericsson, three earphone sets, which meant that I had -- I was issued with them on behalf of the entire group in charge of the security of the president. With the administration of the group about the sector for the security of the president in the presence of two inspectors, in July we handed over all means that I owed to the Ministry of Interior with regards to all means or equipment that I was owing, so to speak, the ministry in order to equip the group. As I said in my statement previously, when I was questioned by the Defence, in the list of phones I was issued with, I have three or four -- there are three or four under my name, but it was not me using them. So, obviously, this is improper management of the administration in the Ministry of Interior; and, due to this reason, I can't return something that I don't have the possession of. And I said, precisely, in my request that you read out, that with regards to all necessary documents and all equipment, I indicated what my address was, what my ID card number was, my home number, and my mobile phone number. These are data contained in my application. Never has anyone from the Ministry of Interior gotten in touch with me with regard to this data. But if you read further, this letter that you are now present to go me, please kindly read it out before the Chamber. Read the remaining portion of the text, where it says that the ministry has no right to hold on my employment booklet. So the Ministry of Interior was not upholding the law, consciously Do you believe that the Ministry of Interior should violate the law?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, Mr. Keskovski, that if the Ministry of Interior held onto your booklet, then it was your right to hold on to their equipment? Is that what you're suggesting by your last statement?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that a committee was established, and the equipment was handed over to the sector for security of president in July 2002, June or July 2002. The Ministry of Interior had records in the finance sector. This means that they should present evidence that I was still owing this equipment. This is not an evidence, this is not a proof that I was owing the equipment, because an evidence should be enclosed, the issuance list with my signature. The Ministry of Interior could indicate that I-- I also owe a hand-rocket launcher or a tank, but this would not be the truth. Due to these reasons, I addressed them and I asked to reconcile our demands to level that, but this hasn't been done. The only demand that I had received were 400 or 600 dollars which are a contentious matter because the ministry has sent a petition, but that was also disputed because we -- two Official Notes are not present, and they should be part of the evidence there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you mention in your request to the ministry in June 2005 that or did you tell them that you didn't have this equipment, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I turn the page, and let's read the letter. It is stated there precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the letter I'm referring to is your request in 2005. It's at page 13 of your booklet.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it here in Macedonian. Could I be shown it on the display --

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: It's ERN --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- so that I'm able to read it in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's ERN N006-7443, if we can please have that displayed in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have indicated precisely: "With regards to any additional demand you have in relation to my case, please inform me in a timely fashion at my personal address or the telephone indicated here," and I have also given my mobile phone number, which means I have not avoided any obligations that they believed I had. I am speaking here, again, about their demands, not demands that are realistic. I can't restore something that I haven't had. If I had an automatic gun, the Ministry of Interior would find it illegal possession of weapons. This is an incrimination under the Criminal Code of the Republic of Macedonia. That would mean that the Ministry of Interior will make a search of my premises and will move to have these weapons confiscated. This is it not a request to restore a pen or a pencil, so obviously they had problems with their demands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I simply wanted to indicate that, in our view, Your Honour, the question is quite unfair, at least the way it was phrased, asking the witness whether he had referred to that particular letter or request in his own letter. He has indicated on a number of occasion that he did not receive that information, and it is actually explicitly mentioned in the information itself. And if Your Honour would turn to page 18 of this same file, there's a note or an information which specifically states that the warning sent to inter alia Mr. Keskovski were returned back as of the wrong addresses. So, in our submission, Your Honour, the suggestion which the Prosecution is making that Mr. Keskovski would have been aware of the content of that information or request is inaccurate and wrong, based on the information contained in this file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness had already mentioned that he had not received them, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Keskovski, to be perhaps more precise, is when you did finally -- when contact was finally made with the Ministry of Interior, and you informed them of your cellular phone number and your contact details, you didn't actually indicate in that letter that you didn't have any property that belonged to the ministry, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an application I'm making to have my employment booklet back, and this is not meant to justify whether I have any property that I'm holding on to. So there is nothing to respond to when they have not requested anything from me. When I called them on the phone, they told me that there is a petition against me, and that until this is resolved, they will not give my employment booklet to me, and that is in breach of the labour law. So I conferred with my attorney, and we sent two such letters to the Ministry of Interior where we cite to the labour law. I really am presently involved in a court procedure which is the legal way of communication between two parties that have a dispute regarding their demands. A unilateral document could not be valid in trials, in hearings in the courts of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski--

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the reasons why I asked that my legal rights are respected. Yes, please go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I will stop you there because I think you have gone beyond answering the question. What did you mean earlier when you said that the Ministry of Interior had to level and reconcile your demands? You and the minister of the interior had to reconcile or level your demands, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly this: For all your other requests or claims. They did not inform me at all about their requests. They said that there was a petition, and you can see this with the legal sector at the ministry. And while the petition was ongoing, they would not return my employment booklet. I did not receive personally any such claims. I did not sign, nor was it submitted to me. It's the same as the decision which you showed me. This is not one which I signed. My letter has my signature, and I can attest to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So your position, if I can put it in a nutshell, is that the ministry, after having sent all these letters to you, demanding that you return the equipment, is simply wrong in that you kept any of this equipment. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on anything which the ministry has undertaken. I can comment about my actions. I do not have such things with me. There is a commission; and, in the course of 2002, the reconciliation was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Moving, then, on to another topic. When you worked with the -- as the assistant to the DBK sector, part of your duties were -- was to collect or gather information. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And part of your duties was to write reports. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My task was assistant director for operative works, which means that I received information which I had to read to be on top of the work and to be able to consult with the director. If I had understanding of some kind, then these were with reports, as well as all other employees at the Ministry of Interior. All employees at the MOI have the task, when obtaining certain information, to send a note about them, which will be further forwarded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So you reviewed the reports of other employees. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And in your review of these reports that related to operative matters, as you say, you had to be as careful and as accurate as possible in attempting to see whether or not all the relevant information was placed in these reports, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you refer to operative works, Mr. Keskovski, are you referring to matters that are of a criminal nature?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: All knowledge regarding perpetrated crimes which pertain to the domain of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So that would relate to serious matters or serious criminal activity that was being investigated by the DBK, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And, therefore, it would be important to be as careful, detailed, and accurate in ensuring that the relevant information regarding a particular investigation was made or was written in -- in the reports, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Prior to this coming to us, this would have to be done already.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But you, as the supervisor, had the overall responsibility to ensure the accuracy and detail in these reports, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I know in my office whether these are relevant or not? The relevance has to be established previously. This is information gained on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But this is information that you may receive from your subordinates as to the -- what was being carried out in a particular investigation and what may have seemed relevant in a particular investigation of criminal activity; and you may have some input, therefore, in the reports that your subordinates were preparing. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have subordinates at the Ministry of Interior while working with the UBK [as interpreted]. Therefore, this is not control over my subordinates. The UBK [as interpreted] had heads of sectors, and they were directly responsible to the director of the directorate for security and counter-intelligence. I was the assistant to the director, which does not, in turn, mean that I had subordinates in the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But, nevertheless, you've told us that part of your job was to review these reports, so you had some responsibility over their content; and as assistant to the director of the DBK, that was a pretty important position, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This position, generally speaking, is entitled "assistant" which should be no the office of the director. It is not a very high-level position, a very senior position in the UBK [as interpreted] because all senior positions, according to the hierarchy, is in the hands of the head of the sector who are directly responsible for the director. Therefore, my competencies did not include subordinates. I only read the reports; and if I had certain comment, I made comments on them with the director.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But you were conscious and careful in your work, were you -- or I should say, were you conscious and careful in carrying out your tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you compile reports for the director based on reports that you received from other members of the DBK?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not part of my work tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But when you received the reports from other members of the DBK, did you read the reports carefully?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reports which I received were also received by the director of the directorate. I was not the filter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: -- that wasn't my question. My question was: When you received these reports, did you read them carefully. It's a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you're asking me now, the answer to this is yes. I read them carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you check the reports for problems or mistakes that needed to be followed up weapon you read them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not read many reports so that I can respond to you more specifically on this question. I was on this position for a very short period of time --

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in which you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: -- that wasn't my question. My question was: The reports that did you read, during the time when you were the assistant to the director of the DBK, did you check the reports for problems or mistakes that may have needed following up.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask that 65 ter 1290, please, be displayed on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And for your purposes, Mr. Keskovski, this would be at tab 1 of the Prosecution binder.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Binder 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, binder 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can ask the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please give me a moment. I'm fine. Just please direct me to where I should be turning. Please point out the tab which I should be looking at.
