utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I will momentarily, Mr. Keskovski. Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can just ask for 65 ter 1290, the OTP statement of Mr. Keskovski, to please be displayed on the e-court screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Keskovski, if I can draw your attention to the document that's displayed on your screen, which is also found at tab 1 in the binder. Is that your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you look at the very bottom of the page, that's -- is that your signature on the bottom of the -- of the page?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And that first page described your particulars. It has your name, your date of birth, and it also indicates that the languages that were spoken during the course of the statement include your language, Macedonian, and English. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And the language that was used was Macedonian and English. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And you actually speak English pretty -- quite well. Is that right, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: We saw a diagram that had you drawn earlier, and, in fact, you draw the diagram in English, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can please ask for the next page to be displayed on the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, is that your signature at the bottom and your initials?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask for the next page, please, to be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And that's your signature as well, at the bottom of that page, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask for the following page to be displayed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: That's your signature as well?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask for the following page, then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And that's your signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That is N001-4889, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Right, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can show all the pages successively.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you please identify your signature. You have, in fact, perhaps to speed things up, you have signed every page in this statement, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can please show the last page of the statement -- actually, if we can show the last signature page, it's N001-4898. It's the previous page, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, that's your signature dated 7 February 2005, and this is signed at the bottom of the witness acknowledgment which reads: "This statement, consisting of 15 pages, has been read over to me in the Macedonian language and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection. "I have given this statement voluntarily and am aware that it may be used in legal proceedings before the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia for the prosecution of persons responsible for serious violations of the international law committed in the former Yugoslavia. I am also aware that I may be called to give evidence in public before the Tribunal." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And that's your signature at the bottom, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: When you gave your statement, Mr. Keskovski, did you try to be as truthful and as accurate as possible?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered to all questions posed by the investigator, and I think I was pretty elaborate in my answers. I did not refuse to answer any of the questions I was asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: That wasn't my question, Mr. Keskovski. My question was: When you gave this statement and you signed it, did you try to be as truthful and as accurate as possible?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You knew that the investigators were investigating a serious criminal matter into the events in Ljuboten when they interviewed you, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You were careful in providing your answers to questions, were you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, about the questions which I was asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And you didn't want to leave any important details out of your responses or your answers, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had not forgotten anything on purpose. I feel that I have not omitted anything or forgotten anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And this statement was given in 2005, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So the events in question would have been fresher in your mind at that stage than perhaps they are today. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me, it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned in your examination-in-chief that Ljube Boskoski was the best man at your wedding. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the best man at my wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Being someone's best man, particularly in your culture, is very significant, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, it's also very significant on a -- from a personal relationship perspective, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And you were quite close to Ljube Boskoski, which is why you picked him as your best man, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew each other well. We were not very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, you say that you continue to have a relationship with Ljube's family, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since then onward, then one could say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that you're quite close to Ljube Boskoski and his family. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have good relations -- a good relationship, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, in fact, you have a pretty important relationship, given that he was your best man at your wedding, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you speaking now about Mr. Boskoski or his family? The relationship between Mr. Boskoski and myself, or my relationship with his family?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm referring to the relationship between Mr. Boskoski and yourself.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no contact with Mr. Boskoski because currently, or since August 2004, he is in the prison in Scheveningen, of your Court, in the Tribunal. I do have a relationship with -- with the family, of course with the wife of Mr. Boskoski and three underaged children who are in Macedonia alone. I contact with them from time to time to see whether they need anything or how they're doing as a family.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And you continued your contact and your relationship with Mr. Boskoski's family because of your relationship and your friendship with Mr. Boskoski. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You said that you picked Mr. Boskoski as your best man at your wedding because you believed him to be an honest person. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Would you consider yourself, Mr. Keskovski, an honest person?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is part of my code of behaviour which I have been adhering to for the past 31 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So, as an honest person, you wouldn't try -- you wouldn't lie or attempt to evade questions that are being asked of you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to now move on to another topic. In your examination-in-chief, you've explained that the sector for security for the president was a unit within the Ministry of Interior. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if we can please display the diagram that the witness drew and referred to yesterday, 65 ter 9.2, on to the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I may be wrong; but if the Prosecutor is trying to show, that must be the other diagram, I understand, and it would be Exhibit 1D317, if my understanding is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for the assistance. It should be 65 ter 9.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, as -- now you drew this diagram which depicts, as you explained, the organisation of your sector as it was organised in 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And it was you, as head of the sector, who decided how the sector should be organised. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear, you, as the head of the sector, assigned the two deputies. You picked them as your two deputies, as well as assigned one of the members of the ARM as your assistant. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the two deputies, this was done in consultation with the president. These are the deputies who would follow the president in the case of my absence. They would replace me in carrying out my duties. As for the army, I have no right to request who would be the head from among the rank of the army, because the army, in accordance with the law, the ARM puts someone who was an acquaintance of the president to that position, and I cooperated with him as my tasks obligated me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, we will come to that in a moment, Mr. Keskovski, but it was you who decided which positions each person within your sector should be posted to as the head of the sector. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on each of these positions. I did not put them on -- in all of these positions. There are some very sensitive tasks involved with some of these positions, and these are sometimes of a private nature. After all, this is the security of the president of his person and his family. I was in constant consultation with the president about engaging persons who carry out tasks of a sensitive nature. For the most part, then, the answer is yes, but not all of them. Not all of them were made on the basis of my personal decisions. In some cases, I consulted with the president and I took into account his considerations, which I think is a normal way of communicating.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But, ultimately, it wasn't the president who decided how the sector was to be structured, was it, despite your consultations with him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards to the structure, I was personally responsible how this will be organised, yes. I created it; I implemented it. We're now discussing, and my previous answer pertains to, the appointment of a persons. But with regards to the structure, yes. I appointed the structure; I implemented the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say you implemented the structure, that includes the persons that were, for example, your deputies, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the appointment?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm referring to the way in which you organised and the people that you picked as your deputies within the structure of your sector.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The deputies as we have them here in the chart, as well all the other individuals appointed, apart from the sensitive tasks. As I told you, there were sensitive tasks within the functioning of this sector. We had special training and selection, in cooperation with the American Secret Service or the counter-terrorist training group. In cooperation with them, we had selection, which also involved the president of the state. Naturally --

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the selection was made and the two deputies were appointed. They were members of the professional special unit Tiger.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you keep referring to "we," Mr. Keskovski. But in fact, you, as the head of the sector, made the final decision, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, yes. I can make the final decisions, but still I need to tell you and I have told you several times already. Regarding some issues, I had consultations with the president, so that I can follow his requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, you mentioned that and I would ask you to please answer my questions as directly and precisely as you can, okay? Now you mentioned, Mr. Keskovski, that there were some sensitive issues in dealing with the security matters of the president; and, in fact, the job of security operation is actually a very complex matter that involves more than simply ensuring the personal security of the president as an individual. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to answer briefly or broadly?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I would like you to answer briefly. I'd like to you answer my question.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The security for the president, as I stated answering previous questions relating to this, is a complex matter, which presupposes providing security for the president as institution, not an individual only. It involves many tasks of various nature related to the security and safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And the reason that's it's a complex matter is, in part, this may seem obvious, because the president was a very prominent figure in the country, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So with respect to other prominent figures, such as the prime minister, for example, the organisation and the security relating to other prominent figures is also a complex matter, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And the head of security for the prime minister was Vlatko Stefanovski. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And the head of the president of the parliament security section was someone called "Aco," right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you recall Aco's last name?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember it at the moment. I knew him only as "Aco." I had no contacts with him, as a colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: The head of the security for the Ministry of Interior was Zoran Trajkovski, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And because of the complexity of security relating to prominent figures, such as the president, you, as the head of your sector, would have regular communication with, say, the head of security for the prime minister, for example, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You've never communicated with the head of the security for the prime minister?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rarely, very rarely. When we had some joint official business or events that we covered together, so to say. But very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, when you had these joint official business or events that you covered together, you needed to communicate with other heads, such as the head of security for the prime minister or the head of the security of Minister Boskoski, in order to ensure that your coordinated effort of securing these prominent figures was effective. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During any movement, we called that "movement," or during any operation that needed to happen, when the president of the state was present and the other state officials as well, the security was in charge of the security of the state of the president. Any agreements between various institutions and their security sectors took place between the advances. This is the -- this is a professional expert matter. The advance goes first; and, at the same place, the advance of the prime minister and the advance of the president meet, and then they carry out all tasks necessary for the operation. If someone wishes to have personal contact with me, that would be something else, but I have had never had questions or contacts related to this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, in order for you to carry out what you refer to as advances with -- that may relate to the prime minister, for example, meeting or having -- going to a joint event with the president, surely you would have to communicate with the head of security of the prime minister, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no need. I explained, before every movement, the advance team is at the location at the minimum of two or three hours in advance, depending on the seriousness of the event and the location. It could be that there they are there 48 hours in advance. At the same time, sooner or later, the security of the prime minister has its advance team that has its own tasks, and they coordinate there on the spot between themselves. But, as I said also in the statement previously, the security, if the president is present, the security is in the hands of the security of the president, because the Presidency is highest institution in the state. It could not be that the security of the prime minister guarantees the security and the safety of the president of the state, because the president is the highest institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But because the president is the highest institution, as you say, you would receive and release information, perhaps, regarding other prominent figures that may be present at a particular function or an event that the president is -- is attending. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a matter for the both protocols, and that is not within my realm of competence. If you wish, I can explain precisely how the system works.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Keskovski, that if another prominent figure was present and attending the same function as the president, that you wouldn't have to coordinate your efforts together with other security services? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already that if, at this location where we are now, the president of the state needs to arrive, but at the same time the prime minister of the state needs to arrive, this location here and now is secured by the security, by the security sector of the president, with all measures and necessary activities that need to be undertaken. All other high officials present there at the meeting would be covered by those security measure, regardless of whether they come from Macedonia or abroad. I believe that I had already told you this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Keskovski, wouldn't you be -- wouldn't have you to necessarily communicate with, for example, the heads of these other security services in order to make decisions regarding the security of the president and other figures attending the same function?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, we don't understand one another. I received information with regards to the security situation, regardless of the location. I received information from all relevant services who have been given the task of informing us. So, on the basis of those information, we made decision regarding the strength and the level of security that needs to be achieved at that spot. There was no need for me to have contact with individuals in charge of security of other high officials in the Republic of Macedonia, and that is a fact. I can't tell you that I had contacts when I haven't had contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Would you -- when you say you receive information from all relevant services, would those services include, for example, the local police at an OVR or at the SVR level?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said "other security services." I believe that the translation was not proper. With regards to the information on the security situation, we received the information from services in charge of matters such nature, UBK, intelligence agency, and the sector for security within the Ministry of Defence. With regards to physical and in depth security to a given area, we involved members of the Ministry of Interior, by the same time also members of the Ministry of Defence, at various locations where there was need of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So is my -- is the answer to my question, yes, there are times when you would involve members of the Ministry of Interior, depending on the situation?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did include or services from the Ministry of Interior, the Ministry of Defence as well, when there was a need of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Would you say that the -- the job of a security operation is a creative job, Mr. Keskovski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's a job that, because it involves the protection of the highest member of the state, it would unite other security structures and institutions in the country, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And because of the complexity of the security situation, sometimes, in order to get the job done, leaders like the president had to be creative and flexible. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise in your question? What do you understand under flexible, that they need to be flexible?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, for example, Mr. Keskovski, isn't it true that the reason that your section was manned with men from the military units was because the Ministry of Interior, at that time, was simply unable to provide the manpower? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that, in my statement also given to the investigators, I stated that we had a meeting between the higher instances of the ministries of the interior; assistant to the ministry, Gacovski; and head for security, at that time Dorevski; and the advisor for national security of the president. The advisor requested that the number of security team members within the sector is increased. The Ministry of Interior stated that at the moment they were not able to fulfil this demand, and then the reinforcement was sought from the army. Is this what you wanted to ask me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So the answer to my question, then would, have been "yes." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, We didn't object the first time round to the question. I mean, Mr. Keskovski has asked for clarification of what was meant by that. The basis of or objection also, Your Honour, is that in the original question, which is at line 23 and 24 of page 58, the Prosecutor put the question as "leader like the president." I think my colleague should be more precise. If she wishes to ask about the flexibility or creativity of the president, we would obviously not object to this line of questioning. But if she wishes to ask about other individuals and creativity, I believe the basis should be established first to see whether Mr. Keskovski has any knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't believe that any of my questions were improper, and I think that if Mr. Mettraux needs clarification, he can certainly do so in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Part of the reason, Mr. Keskovski, that your unit needed more men in 2001 was because it was a complex security situation at that time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And to get the job done, they pulled men from the ARM, or the army, and placed them under your command. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were not employed. They were just retained or seconded from the army. There was no new employment. They were placed under my command, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So they were placed under your command, but, as you say, seconded from the army, right? They were placed under your command for the purpose of dealing with matters that related to your sector specifically, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right, with specific tasks related to the security of the president of the Republic of Macedonia and the supreme commander of the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So, with respect to tasks or with respect to, perhaps, tasks that did not relate to the sector of the president, they, men from the ARM, answered to their commanders within the army. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't understand your question, because they were retained only to provide security for the president. They had no other working tasks. So there was no need for them to send reports that are not related to -- there was no task within the remit that is not related to the security of the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But they continued to be employed by the army, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And they received their salary from the army. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I believe that it is written in the order as well, that that is the duty of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So they were still under the army chain of command. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you think that they received orders from the army, then the hierarchy line, no, that is not correct. They were part of the army, but they were placed under the command of the head for security. This was the request of the supreme commander, and it was strictly forbidden that any army reports are sent to the higher structures of the army because of the risk of leaking information that might be of complex nature, and there was no need for the army to be aware of that from a political viewpoint. That is one of the principles of this sector for security, regardless of what members of it are concerned. We had members of the security agency and UBK intelligence agency in order to better coordinate the information relevant for the security and safety of the president of the state, but this did not mean that they needed to send reports relating to all events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Once again, I think that you are evading my questions, and I'd ask you to be brief and precise and direct in your answers.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you did not ask the question correctly. So I would kindly ask you to ask me more specifically, precisely, because your question had sort of a double meaning. So ask the question specifically, and I will answer anything that you wish to learn from me, and I don't wish to avoid any of your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Weren't these men from the ARM ordered or the army ordered to go to the Ministry of Interior by the army?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you understand under "going to the Ministry of Interior"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, they were ordered to go to work within your sector, which is part of the Ministry of Interior. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't say to go to work with the Ministry of Interior. A person works where the contract specifies they work and where they receive the salary from. They were retained by the supreme commander of the armed forces through an order, and they belonged to the units where they received their salary from, but they were placed under the command of the person that the supreme commander specifies in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, they were placed upped your command, and you were part of the Ministry of Interior. Isn't that so? That is a very precise question.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you said were they were going to the ministry, and that is a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have reached time for the second break, Ms. Issa. If the court officer could assist the witness out, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa, we have waited with considerable patience for the whole of that last session, an hour and a half. The Chamber is concerned that a great deal of time is being spent with very little effective productivity. Your questions need to be directed more to the issues directly concerning this case, and the whole process needs to be quicker or else we fear that this cross-examination could be very considerably and unnecessarily prolonged. If you would be good enough to take those comments under consideration and attempt to simply move much more quickly and effectively, we would be grateful. Thank you. We resume now at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, I'm going to move on to another topic now. You mentioned, in your examination-in-chief, that Zivko Gacovski was the chief of the security department in the Ministry of Interior, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zivko Gacovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: He was, in fact, in charged of the security for, not just your sector, but for VIP persons, the minister, the prime minister, and the president. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And for foreign delegation; yes, the foreign delegations as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But you say that you didn't report to him. That was your examination-in-chief, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And that is because you didn't have a good relationship with Zivko Gacovski, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not because of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: But you didn't have a good relationship with Zivko Gacovski, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have good relations -- a good relationship from a professional point of view, not from a private one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And Zivko Gacovski's superiors were the minister of the interior and Goran Mitevski, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, yes, but at a different time, in different positions, according to the systemization. The first time, I believe, he was appointed by the government and was responsible only before the minister. So you have to ask me specifically about the time-frame, and then I can give you a concrete answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean of 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. I will be speaking about 2001 the entire time, and should I change that I will tell you that the time-frame is different, but we're only dealing with matters that relate to 2001. So, at that time, those were Minister Boskoski and Goran Mitevski as his superiors. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the new systemization in the second half of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, although, you didn't communicate or report to Zivko Gacovski, you did communicate, regarding matters that related to your sector, with Minister Boskoski, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our requests from the Ministry of Interior, in regards to this, I communicated with the director for public security, Mr. Goran Mitevski; and in his absence, or when he was absent, I requested the assistance from the minister, Mr. Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And, in fact, you had an excellent relationship or communication with Minister Boskoski, a better one, perhaps, than the one had you with the previous minister, Dosta Dimovska. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is right, and I think I made this statement before the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. And that's because Minister Boskoski was an effective manager, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is because, at the request of the president, we had a meeting between the minister of the interior, the director for public security, and myself to improve the security --

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, my question was: Your relationship with Minister Boskoski, relating to matters in your sector, was a very good one, had an excellent communication, and that was because Minister Boskoski was an effective manager, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can respond "yes" to your question, but I have to elaborate why this is so. You may have one; I have an altogether different opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'm only asking you to respond to my questions, Mr. Keskovski. I appreciate that you may have different opinions. Now, turning to another topic, in 2001, the Ohrid Framework Agreement was scheduled to be signed on 13 August, 2001, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Skopje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: To be signed in Skopje, that's correct. And the president spent a month, from approximately the 25th or the end of July to 10 August, in the course of negotiations regarding the Ohrid Framework Agreement, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And, initially, the president and his entourage, which included you, went to Ohrid with the intention of staying a couple of days. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the right. We went in the middle of July with the intent of staying three days. We stayed as long as you said we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And that was, in part, because the president was under enormous pressure from the international community to reach an agreement to essentially avoid a civil war, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And the president was personally, as far as you know, very concerned about the success of the agreement, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: He worked very hard at ensuring that it was ultimately signed on 13 August, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you've told us, yesterday, in your testimony, that, on the 10th of August, you received some information from Chief of Staff General Stamboliski that an attack had been carried out on the Ljubotenski Bacila mining incident, causing the death of eight soldiers, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You said that at the time you were in the company of the president, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You also said that you passed the phone to the president and the president spoke to General Stamboliski directly and issued him an order, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I handed the telephone over to the president, and the chief of the General Staff conveyed to him what he previously conveyed to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never mentioned anything about an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, you said, Mr. Keskovski, that the president was angry because, as you say - this is at page 60 of yesterday's transcript - that: "We had Karpalak on the 8th where ten members of the Macedonian army died." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Then you said, at page 62 of the transcript, that the president ordered General Stamboliski immediately to send immediate orders to eliminate all terrorist groupations in Macedonia. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the position of the national security council which held a session. At the same time, this is an order of the president for action on the part of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're sure, Mr. Keskovski, that the president issued this order to General Stamboliski in your presence?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now the Karpalak incident occurred on the 8th of August, isn't that so, in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And the Karpalak incident was essentially an incident where the NLA killed ten soldiers that occurred as a retaliation for an operation carried out by the Ministry of Interior forces on the 7th of August. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was retaliation. I can only note that this attack did happen and that the soldiers died, ten soldiers died.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I would ask you to please turn to tab 5 of your binder?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 314.1, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, this is an article, Mr. Keskovski, titled "The Ohrid Framework Agreement Negotiations," by Vasko Popetrevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, for the record, it comes from a book called: "Ohrid and Beyond," published by the Institute for War and Peace reporting in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to what is page N002-1350. It should be page 55 in your hard copy, and the second-to-the-last paragraph in this article on this page refers to the August 7 incident. It says: "The negotiations were finally over and the discussions had moved to the signing protocol when the agreement would be signed, whether it should be signed in Ohrid or Skopje. On August 7, violence intervened. An operation was conducted in a Skopje suburb by the special anti-terrorist unit of the Ministry of Interior." Then it goes on and describes the operation. At the end of that paragraph, it states: "What was immediately obvious was that this incident placed the future of the Ohrid Agreement in jeopardy." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it only in the English language, and I can hear the interpretation to what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. At the bottom of that page, it says that: "'The story was given a full 15 minutes of air time,' said Popovski, adding that the SDSM team were extremely anxious about what would follow. "Within 24 hours," and this is the very last sentence that I'm reading, "Popovski's fears were realised. The next morning, August 8, a lightly armed Macedonian army convoy was ambushed near Karpalak on the Skopje-Tetovo highway," and it describes that nine reservists were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is the following page at the very top at page 56. N002-1351 is the ERN number, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if we see at the very middle paragraph of that page, it describes what took place which led to the initialling of the Ohrid Agreement. It says: "US Envoy Pardew presented the Albanian representatives with a pen and urged them to initial the agreement. Xhaferi and Imeri were reluctant, but Pardew then warned them that tragedy could ensue if they refused. After consulting with the NLA headquarters in Sipkovica and receiving a green light, the PDP and DPA representatives agreed to initial the document. "On the same day, VRMO-DPMNE announced that they were suspending their participation in the dialogue. After the incident at Karpalak, the parties spokesperson declared, 'We cannot be expected to participate in a political dialogue while soldiers are being killed, civilians kidnapped, and there are shoot outs in and around Tetovo.' But later that day, they initialed the document along with the SDSM representatives, and the signing was scheduled for August 13 in Skopje." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So after, the violence of 7 and 8 August, which placed the Ohrid Agreement in jeopardy, the agreement was finally initialed, and there was a signing date scheduled of the 13th of August, and this was the day after the Karpalak incident. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So wouldn't the president be concerned on the 10th of August that further retaliatory action might jeopardize the signing of the Ohrid Agreement, which was scheduled for two days later?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you, Mr. Keskovski, to please turn to paragraph 32 of your statement which is 65 ter 1290, and it's at tab 1 of the Prosecution book of authorities -- or the Prosecution book of exhibits, rather. We can display it on the screen, in you can't find it. It should be at page N001-4892. Do you have it there, paragraph 32 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, when you were asked about returning from Ohrid by the investigators, you said this: "On the 10th of August, 2001, we came back from Ohrid some time in the morning, and the chief of General Staff of the army, General Metodija Stamboliski, called me by phone and informed me about the Ljubotenski Bacila mine incident. Later on, I have passed the information to the president. I understood that, in the mine incident, some soldiers were army got killed, and they were from Ljubanci village." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You agree now, Mr. Keskovski, that you've now told us, in your testimony, that you passed the phone to the president, and General Stamboliski directly provided this information to the president, and the president subsequently issued an order to Stamboliski; but in your statement, you say that you, later on, passed this information to the president. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that on the way from Ohrid, General Stamboliski called. This means that we were together with the president, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, your statement seems to reflect, Mr. Keskovski, that it was you that gave the information to the president, and the president did not speak to General Stamboliski at that time, did he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My statement is that the president directly received or heard the statement made by General Stamboliski. The investigators asked a general question, and I gave my response in a general manner about the 10th of August. So the answer to your question is "yes"; but in the questioning during these sessions, I was asked more specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You would agree with me, Mr. Keskovski, that when you expressly say, "Later on, I passed the information to the president," that's a pretty specific statement, isn't it? There's nothing ambiguous about that, is there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And the president, in fact, if we go to paragraph 34 of your statement, expressed concern about this incident, and he said, according to your statement: "I was present during the conversation with Johan Tarculovski the afternoon of the 10th of August, 2001." And at the bottom of your statement, you say: "I heard the president asking Johan Tarculovski to call the next day and inform the president about the situation in the village. The president was concerned that if there was unrest in the village, it could postpone the signing of the Ohrid Agreement, which was scheduled for Monday, 12 August 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Isn't that what really happened on that day, Mr. Keskovski, that the president was concerned about the unrest as a result of the Ljubotenski mining incident, that he asked for information because he didn't want to delay the Ohrid Agreement? Isn't that what really happened?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I stated, and this is what I'm stating today. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So the president never issued an order to General Stamboliski to take any sort of retaliatory action, did he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The position of the president, and also in the communication with the chief of the General Staff of the Republic of Macedonia, was identical of that -- of the national security counsel, as I said yesterday, to retrieve the position of the 5th of July, as to facilitate the signing of the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that yesterday as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski, my question was: The president did not issue an order to General Stamboliski, according to your statement, to take retaliatory action on that day, on the 10th of August, did he?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president issued an order to General Stamboliski, however, not in the context to undertake retaliatory measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: There's nothing in your statement that says that on the 10th of August, in the context of the Ljubotenski Bacila mining incident, that the president issued an order, is there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the statement I made to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. The statement that you signed, and you told us earlier you tried to be as careful and accurate as possible. That's what we're talking about right now.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement which I gave to the investigator was not specific and concise. I responded in the same manner that I was asked. There were no specific questions and, therefore, this is the statement I made and I stand behind it still.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, on page 70 of your transcript, and you just repeated today, you said that when you were in the car on your way to Skopje from Ohrid, that you immediately informed the president regarding the Ljubotenski Bacila mining incident. That's what you said in your testimony, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if you informed the president while you were in the car at that time, why does it say here, at paragraph 34 in your statement, that, "In the afternoon of 10 August 2001, the president approved the request and asked me to call Johan Tarculovski. As I called him, the president wanted to speak to him. I gave him the phone and I heard the president asking Johan Tarculovski to call the next day and inform the president about the situation in the village"? It goes on to say how concerned he was about the unrest postponing the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: My question is: If that's what happened, why would the president wait until the afternoon to call or just to mention this, if, in fact, you immediately informed the president while you were in the car?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about two different situations, one involving Tarculovski and the other involves General Stamboliski. They are not one and the same. The situation with General Stamboliski transpired in the morning because the incident happened in the morning, and immediately the president was informed. With regards to Mr. Tarculovski, he phoned later. Of course, the information took time to arrive to him, so it is not the same situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if that is the case and you informed the president while you were in the car and the president spoke to General Stamboliski, why does it say in your statement that, "Later on, I passed the information to the president"?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Later" denotes time. I immediately communicated the information to him, and he immediately spoke to General Stamboliski. I was riding in the car with him. I will repeat again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered to the investigator's questions in the same fashion that they were asked. They were not specific enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You didn't tell the investigators at that time that the president spoke to General Stamboliski and he issued General Stamboliski an order, did you? It's a very specific question.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered as he asked me, and this is now the content of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: The information that you gave Mr. Stamboliski [sic] is pretty specific, though, isn't it? The information that you gave the investigator about how you received the information and how you passed it on to the president is quite specific, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such information came and were communicated to the president every day. In this specific case, it is as I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you. The information that you gave the investigator in your statement, particularly at paragraph 32, as to how you passed information on to the president or how you received it regarding the mining incident, is specific, isn't it? That remembers a "yes" or "no" answer.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I communicated the information to the president, but he also spoke directly to the head -- to the chief of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I was asking about the information that you communicated to the investigator, and now you're giving us a different answer, aren't you? You didn't tell us before that you communicated the information to the president. You said you passed the phone on to the president, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It never happens when somebody informed me about something. I briefed the president first, and then I passed the phone to him so that he knew he was to talk about. This is standard. It happens every day. This was not an isolated event. This is something that happens every day. So in all cases, with information of this nature, but also with information of ordinary nature, this is the procedure that I always followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you this question one last time, Mr. Keskovski. You did not give this information about the president speaking to General Stamboliski to the investigator of the OTP when you gave your statement, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president --

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Mr. Keskovski --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- received such very --

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: -- I am going to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- delicate questions, personally. I just can't communicate those to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the president. I'm asking the information you gave the investigator that is in your statement. I've asked you that question several times now.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you kindly repeat the question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: You did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do that, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm grateful, and I know the dislike of the Chamber to interrupt. But I believe at this stage the witness has been asked several times the same question, and he has given a very clear answer. Everyone can see for themselves that what is or is not in the statement. I believe he has given the explanation as to why something may or not be in them. I believe that asking him the same question several times serves no purpose and could be unfair to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are assured this is the last time, Mr. Mettraux, so we will be a little more patient. Carry on, please, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just trying to get a clear answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, there's a point when you can accept that you're not going to get what you want and move on. We can discern what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you answer that question for the last time, Mr. Keskovski, please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked you to kindly repeat the question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: The question was: You did not tell the investigator when you gave your statement that the president allegedly gave an order to General Stamboliski on the 10th of August after he received the information regarding the mining incident, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. I answered the question I was asked and that alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also said, in your testimony, at page 70 from yesterday's transcript, that you invited Johan to Skopje after he requested time off because it was standard procedure to do so. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: And you also said that the president ordered Johan to go to Ljubanci to inform on the developments there, in page 72 of your transcript. Do you recall telling us that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he gave him the order, when he went to use the leave that he requested and was granted, to use that opportunity to inform about the developments in the area of the village of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Didn't you specifically say, in your testimony, that he ordered him to go to Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, and I'm saying it again today, and it is also part of my statement, Mr. Tarculovski requested leave of absence because his close relative was killed, which meant that he would have gone to Ljubanci at any rate. The president ordered him to inform him about the situation and developments while he was already at Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Where does it say, in your statement that you gave the investigators, Mr. Keskovski, that you and the president invited Johan Tarculovski to Skopje after he requested his leave to attend the funeral?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I stated that Johan Tarculovski requested leave of absence to go to a funeral of someone close to him, and that he requested it, yes, on the 10th. In my statement to the investigator, but also here, I say that the standard procedure used, not only in the case of Mr. Tarculovski, but with all others, the president wanted to express personal condolences to every member of his security staff who had lost someone close to him, who have had someone close to him killed in the crisis in 2001. So, for this reason, Mr. Tarculovski was invited to the office. The president personally extended his condolences. And during the conversation - I said then; I'm saying it now - he gave him the task. He ordered him, when going to the funeral, to be there and to inform him about the situation, developments in the area of Ljubanci village. And in the statement, I will repeat again, in the statement to the investigator, I have answered the questions asked of me. The question was not asked precisely. As it was asked, I answered it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that the president met with Johan Tarculovski and at that point told him that, when he goes out to Ljubanci, to provide him with information as to the developments in the village. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat it again because you're twisting my words. The president expressed the condolences to Mr. Tarculovski. We granted him leave of absence for several days so that he attends the funeral at the village of Ljubanci, and he gave him the order to inform him from there, from where he goes to the funeral, to inform him about the situation on the grounds, what was happening in the area of village of Ljubanci. Is this the answer you're requesting from me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: My question is, Mr. Keskovski: Did this take place when you say the president met Johan Tarculovski in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two --

utterances.speaker: MR. ISSA
utterances.text: -- I think you have answered the question. I'd like to draw your attention to paragraph 34 of your statement, which is on the same page as paragraph 32. I think you have it in front of you. Now you see there it says: "In the afternoon of the 10th of August, the president approved the request and asked me to call Johan Tarculovski. As I called him, the president wanted to speak to him, so I gave him the mobile phone. I was present during the conversation, and I heard the president asking Johan Tarculovski to call the next day and inform the president about the situation in the village." You agree with me, Mr. Keskovski, that there's nothing in there that says the president gave him this order in Skopje and that he met with him personally, is there? This is a very specific question, and I'd like a brief answer, please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATKO KESKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is your comment on that. I'm saying here, previously, that he gave him the task, and that would be an order, to Mr. Tarculovski, to phone and inform him about the situation in Ljuboten; but, on the other hand, they met twice. Actually, once they spoke on the phone and then they met next. The president and Tarculovski spoke twice in the same day; once over the phone and once in person.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm conscious of the time, Your Honour.
